rubric: ~/claude-viz/vqa-rubric.md axes 2 and 6 + rise direction; compared against user sample craft (structure only)
pack: /tmp/jps/r24 (1x/3x scene next to station art, 4x sheets)
verdictText:
PIECE 1 jp-overpass-stair-e: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct yes
  - [minor] The east outer rail starts about one tread lower than the west rail, and a 2px grey stub sticks out past the frame where the rail meets the landing. It looks like a leftover pixel rather than a rail end. -> End the east rail with the same 1px dark cap the west rail has, at the landing's south edge, and delete the protruding stub.
  - [minor] All 13 treads repeat the same light, mid and dark band with no change, so the climb is only shown by the landing at the top. -> Add a 1px darker stringer wedge to the outer side rails that widens toward the north. Alternatively, darken the dark riser band slightly on the lowest 3–4 treads.
  - [minor] The diamond mesh has the same value everywhere. It is flatter than the reference landing, where light and dark lattice rows alternate. -> Make every other diagonal row one shade darker so the mesh reads as a raised grating.
PIECE 2 jp-overpass-stair-w: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct yes
  - [minor] Same rail-start mismatch and stub as piece 1, mirrored onto the west side. -> Same fix, mirrored.
PIECE 3 jp-overpass-deck-red: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct n/a
  - [minor] The lighter worn band is barely different from the rest of the deck at 1x. -> Lighten the walk band one more step, and keep the raised dots on it one shade brighter than the dots off it.
  - [minor] The road shadow is a hard-edged, opaque grey rectangle that does not take the road's colour. -> Use a darker shade of the road colour and give the shadow a 1px dithered top edge under the girder.
PIECE 4 jp-side-stair-l: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct yes
  - [minor] Each slab has a full light rim on all four sides of its top, so the run looks like a row of separate posts or bars rather than one connected flight. -> Remove the light rim on each slab's east (inner) side so it butts directly onto the dark outline of the next, taller slab. Keep the light cap row on the north side only.
  - [minor] The outermost slab's face is only the yellow nosing line, with no dark south face under it. It looks like it is floating rather than sitting on the ground. -> Add a 1–2px dark face row under the outer slab's nosing.
PIECE 5 jp-stage-platform: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct n/a
  - [minor] The wood has a slightly olive tint and lower contrast than the rest of the jp_city palette. -> Shift the plank midtone toward warm brown and add one darker seam shade between boards.
  - [minor] Where the stage is used without side stairs, the cut west and east ends show no side face. -> Supply end-cap variants with a 1px dark side outline and the block face wrapping round the corner.
PIECE 6 jp-side-stair-r: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct yes
  - [minor] Same post-like light rims and floating outer slab as piece 4, mirrored. -> Same fixes, mirrored.
PIECE 7 jp-wall-ladder: reads-as-described yes; rise-direction correct yes
  - [minor] The rungs are nearly the same value as the rails, so they look flatter than the existing tunnel ladder. -> Give the rungs a 1px light top edge and a dark underside.
SCENE: - [minor] The deck is clearly raised (girder face, columns, shadow), but the stairs and landings cast no shadow and have no supports, so the landings look ground-level next to the raised deck. -> Add a 1-cell dithered shadow down the east side of each stair and one support column under the outer corner of each landing.
  - [minor] The ladder on the station wall ends under the eave and leads nowhere visible. -> Either end it at a roof hatch or edge drawn on the eave, or place it where it reaches a reachable roof.
  - [minor] The inner side-stair slabs overlap the stage's bottom plank row with no outline between stone and wood. -> Add a 1px dark outline where each slab meets the stage.
  - No piece looks traced from the reference. The overpass stairs follow the same general layout as the reference (mesh landing on top, two lanes), but the palette, rails and pixel work differ.
AXIS2 score 8, AXIS6 score 8
MAJORS TOTAL: 0
